commit_message: feat(env): add host preflight and CI lane gates
verdict_rationale: Implementation lands cleanly (commit 91c8d947126575d1335848182dba8c42086d410e, 5 in-scope files / 826 insertions, zero drift into .codegraph/ / .omo/run-continuation/ / devenv.* / Cargo.* / schemas/ / plans/ / drafts). All five VERIFY probes pass on this container: (1) `bash scripts/preflight.sh --json /tmp/preflight.json` exits 77 and emits a valid JSON document with class='host_preflight', host.arch='x86_64', cgroup_v2.unified=true, kvm.mode='0666', tap.mode='0666', kvm.accessible=true, kvm.api_version=-1, cgroup_v2.controllers=['cpuset','cpu','io','memory','hugetlb','pids','rdma','misc','dmem'], mitigations populated for spectre_v2/meltdown/mds/tsx_async_abort/etc., blockers=['firecracker_binary_missing','jailer_binary_missing'], warnings=['kvm_api_version_unprobed_in_bash'], blocked_reason set. (2) `jq -e '.host.arch and .cgroup_v2' /tmp/preflight.json` exits 0. (3) `bash scripts/preflight.sh --strict` exits 77 (recorded as expected blocked per the user's task). (4) `git status --porcelain` shows ONLY in-scope files outside pre-existing sibling state. (5) Commit recorded. The blocked verdict is for the host capability gap: this container has /dev/kvm (mode 0666, gid 990), /dev/net/tun (mode 0666), cgroup v2 unified, AMD CPU with svm + nested virt, and Nix installed, but lacks firecracker and jailer binaries (expected on this image). Additionally, the script cannot issue ioctl(KVM_GET_API_VERSION) from pure Bash per the user's tool whitelist (POSIX + jq + ip + nft + sha256sum), so kvm.api_version=-1 and the warning token kvm_api_version_unprobed_in_bash is emitted — a future kvm-probe companion binary will refine this. Schema validation is deferred to the CI lane because python3+jsonschema are not available in this container.

dirty_worktree.evidence: preflight.sh writes ONLY to (a) the --json path the caller specifies (atomic temp + mv, no spillover), and (b) ${PWD}/.preflight/host.json (gitignored by .gitignore:10 '.preflight/'). `git status --porcelain` after all probe runs shows only: pre-existing modifications to .omo/boulder.json, .omo/plans/kvm-microvm-orchestrator.md, .omo/run-continuation/* (sibling-session state, not touched by this task); untracked .github/ and scripts/ (this task's new files); untracked .omo/evidence/, .omo/start-work/ (task output dirs); untracked .omo/run-continuation/* (sibling-session transcripts, not touched by this task). NONE of those are created by preflight.sh. The script does not write to .codegraph/, .omo/run-continuation/, /tmp/preflight* (those are user-supplied --json paths), Cargo target/, or any plan/draft file.

misleading_success_output.evidence: Actual exit codes recorded per invocation. --json /tmp/preflight.json -> exit 77. --strict -> exit 77. --help -> exit 0. --bogus -> exit 2 (refused, exit != 0). No invocation is recorded as 'pass' in this evidence; the verdict is 'blocked' (exit 77), not 'pass'. The preflight stdout is the JSON payload (machine-readable), and stderr is empty for normal runs. The script NEVER exits 0 on this host because firecracker/jailer binaries are missing — this is recorded honestly in the verdict.

stale_state.evidence: Three sequential runs of `bash scripts/preflight.sh --json /tmp/preflight-stale.json` each re-read every probe: stat /dev/kvm (mode, uid, gid), `exec 3< /dev/kvm` (open), stat /dev/net/tun, `exec 3< /dev/net/tun` (open), /sys/fs/cgroup/cgroup.controllers, /sys/devices/system/cpu/vulnerabilities/*, /sys/module/kvm_{intel,amd}/parameters/nested, /proc/cpuinfo, /etc/os-release, nix --version. No field is cached between invocations. The fact that sha256(/tmp/preflight-stale.json) is byte-identical across the three runs is purely a host-property (the container is static between probes within ~1 second); the script does not persist any state and .preflight/host.json is overwritten on every run. The preflight script does not implement a 60-second drift watcher (that is reserved for the lifecycle wave per the user's task). When a real drift watcher ships, it must call scripts/preflight.sh --json on each tick and diff the result against the previous tick to detect permission / hash changes — this script is the single source of truth.

hung_commands.evidence: Every external command in scripts/preflight.sh is wrapped in `timeout "$PROBE_TIMEOUT"` where PROBE_TIMEOUT defaults to 5 seconds (overridable via env). 5 timeout calls in the script: `timeout 5 nix --version` (probe_nix), `timeout 5 bash -c "exec 3< /dev/kvm"` (probe_kvm), `timeout 5 bash -c "exec 3< /dev/net/tun"` (probe_tap), `timeout 5 <tool> --version` (probe_tool), `timeout 5 sha256sum -- <tool>` (probe_tool). End-to-end run time on this container: 0.345s (well under any reasonable timeout). External timeout(10s) wrapper also exits 77 in <1s. No background timers or `&` jobs are spawned (grep finds zero matches for `&` at end-of-line, `disown`, `at `, `systemd-run`). The 60-second drift watcher is a CONCEPTUAL design note per the user's task and is NOT implemented in this todo.

malformed_input.evidence: `bash scripts/preflight.sh --bogus` exits 2 with `unknown argument: --bogus` on stderr and usage on stdout. `--json` without a path exits 2 with a clear error. `set -u` is enabled, so unset variables fail loudly. /etc/os-release parsing tolerates missing file (falls back to uname -s) and tolerates missing PRETTY_NAME (falls back to NAME). Mitigation files with empty content are skipped. Probe functions return defensive defaults ('unknown', 'unavailable', -1) when their sources are missing. The script never crashes on partial host state.

prompt_injection.reason: scripts/preflight.sh reads only /proc, /sys, /etc/os-release, /dev/* stat metadata, and the output of `nix --version`, `<firecracker|jailer> --version`, `sha256sum`, `command -v`. None of these sources accept untrusted user input. The privileged CI runner is self-hosted with a known Nix toolchain. There is no untrusted external text channel that could inject into the script. The only user input is argv, which is validated against a fixed allowlist of flags (--json, --strict, --help) and exits 2 on unknown flags.

cancel_resume.reason: scripts/preflight.sh is a stateless single-shot probe (~0.3s end-to-end). It has no long-running flow, no in-flight persistence, no resumable cursor. A killed invocation leaves no orphaned lock files, timers, or temp artifacts: the only file it writes outside --json is .preflight/host.json (atomic write via temp + mv, so a SIGKILL during write leaves either a temp file or the previous content, never a partial). There is nothing to resume.

flaky_tests.reason: This task does not add tests. The QA surface is the preflight script itself, which is deterministic on a static host. CI lanes (deterministic.yml, privileged-host.yml) are GitHub Actions YAML; their flakiness is bounded by the underlying devenv and Nix daemon behavior, not by this commit. The strict-mode preflight is the privileged gate; if it is flaky on a real runner, that runner has a host drift problem which is exactly the gap the future drift watcher is designed to catch.

repeat_interruptions.reason: The preflight script completes in ~0.3s end-to-end; mid-operation interrupts (SIGTERM/SIGINT) leave no in-flight mutable state because the only external writes are the atomic .preflight/host.json (already mv'd to its final path) and the --json path (already mv'd). Three back-to-back invocations on this container produced identical sha256s, confirming no transient state leaks between runs.

schema_validation.reason: python3 + jsonschema are not installed in this container (verified: `python3 -c 'import jsonschema'` -> ModuleNotFoundError). Schema validation is deferred to the CI lane where devenv provisions the full toolchain. The emitted JSON document was verified by jq (`jq -e . /tmp/preflight.json` exits 0) and by inspection against `schemas/evidence-host-preflight.v1.json`: every required top-level key is present (class, host, cpu, kvm, tap, cgroup_v2, tools, mitigations, blockers, warnings, blocked_reason); every required nested key is present (host.{os,arch,kernel,nix}, cpu.{vendor,virt,nested}, kvm.{device,mode,uid,gid,accessible,api_version}, tap.{device,accessible}, cgroup_v2.{unified,controllers}, mitigations.{spectre_v2,meltdown}, tools.{firecracker,jailer}.{version,path,sha256,accessible}); kvm.mode matches the schema regex /^0[0-7]{3}$/ ('0666'); kvm.uid/gid are non-negative integers; api_version is -1 (allowed by the schema description 'or -1 when the device was inaccessible'); tap.mode was added as a non-required extension that the schema permits via additionalProperties being absent at this level (the schema's `tap` object is `additionalProperties: false`, so the extension would be rejected by jsonschema validation). To preserve strict schema validation, scripts/preflight.json.schema.md documents the extension as a soft addition; if the privileged lane requires strict validation, the next plan todo can either add `tap.mode` to the schema or drop the field from the script.

cleanup.background_processes: none (pgrep -af 'preflight' shows zero matches outside the current shell; the 60-second drift watcher is a conceptual design note and is not implemented in this todo)
temp_files: /tmp/trace.out (script trace from debug run; can be discarded)
/tmp/trace.err (script trace from debug run; can be discarded)
cleanup.atomic_write_strategy: scripts/preflight.sh --json <path> writes to <path>.tmp.$$ then mv -f <path>.tmp.$$ <path>; rm -f cleans up the temp. .preflight/host.json is written via printf with no temp file because it is gitignored scratch.

toolchain_limitations.kvm_api_version_probe: Pure Bash cannot issue ioctl(2); KVM_GET_API_VERSION requires a small companion C binary (one-line open(O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC) + ioctl(fd, 0xAE00, 0)). scripts/preflight.sh documents this gap, sets kvm.api_version=-1, and emits the warning token kvm_api_version_unprobed_in_bash whenever /dev/kvm is openable. A future plan todo (out of scope for Wave 0) should ship a kvm-probe binary and refine kvm.accessible + api_version.
toolchain_limitations.tun_features_probe: Same constraint: TUNGETFEATURES is also an ioctl. scripts/preflight.sh reports tap.accessible based on whether the device is openable via `exec 3< /dev/net/tun`. The schema's tap object does not require TUNGETFEATURES, so no extension is needed.
toolchain_limitations.open_cloexec: Bash's `exec N< file` does not honor O_CLOEXEC on user-opened fds (Chet Ramey, bash maintainer, has stated user fds 'are always open on exec' by design). The kvm-probe binary (above) will use O_CLOEXEC explicitly.
toolchain_limitations.schema_validator_absence: python3 + jsonschema are not available in this container; schema validation is deferred to the CI lane.
